text: past two decades, Organization Economic Co-operation Development (OECD) conducted PISA test. goal test evaluate compare educational systems across countries measuring 15-year-old school students’ scholastic performance math, science, reading. country participates given year draw sample least 5,000 students tested. Every three years, OECD publishes international league tables ranking countries performance according PISA test scores. example, use publicly available data 2018 PISA test examine countries best worst math. restrict attention OECD countries. First, load package csranks. Second, load data take quick look : PISA study’s math scores stored math_score. test scores estimated random sample students country. standard errors scores stored math_se. following graph shows raw math scores 95% marginal confidence intervals:  function irank() can used produce integer ranks based math scores: Japan ranked first (.e., best), Korea ranked second . text: First, interested finding countries among top-5 terms true math score. function cstaubest answers question. requires argument estimate covariance matrix test scores. example, reasonable assume estimates different countries mutually independent, covariance matrix diagonal: function cstaubest can used compute 95% confidence set top-5: confidence set contains 12 countries: probability approximately 0.95, 12 countries among top-5 according true math score. According estimated test scores, countries Japan, Korea, Estonia, Netherlands, Poland top-5 countries. However, due statistical uncertainty ranking, uncertainty countries truly among top-5. confidence set shows countries among top-4 (probability approximately 95%). lower required level confidence, confidence set top-5 shrinks: 90% level, can now exclude Sweden among top-5.
code: math_cov_mat <- diag(pisa2018$math_se^2) CS_5best <- cstaubest(pisa2018$math_score, math_cov_mat, tau = 5, coverage = 0.95)  pisa2018[CS_5best, "jurisdiction"] #>  [1] "Belgium"     "Canada"      "Denmark"     "Estonia"     "Finland"     #>  [6] "Japan"       "Korea"       "Netherlands" "Poland"      "Slovenia"    #> [11] "Sweden"      "Switzerland" CS_5best_90 <- cstaubest(pisa2018$math_score, math_cov_mat, tau = 5, coverage = 0.9)  pisa2018[CS_5best_90, "jurisdiction"] #>  [1] "Belgium"     "Canada"      "Denmark"     "Estonia"     "Finland"     #>  [6] "Japan"       "Korea"       "Netherlands" "Poland"      "Slovenia"    #> [11] "Switzerland"

text: Suppose \(j=1,\ldots,p\) populations (e.g., schools, hospitals, political parties, countries) ranked according measure \(\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_p)\). observe true values \(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_p\). Instead, population, data estimated measures, \(\hat{\theta}=(\hat{\theta}_1,\ldots,\hat{\theta}_p)\). values \(\hat{\theta}_1,\ldots,\hat{\theta}_p\) estimates true values \(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_p\) thus contain statistical uncertainty. consequence, ranking populations values \(\hat{\theta}_1,\ldots,\hat{\theta}_p\) contains statistical uncertainty necessarily equal true ranking \(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_p\). function computes confidence sets rank one, several populations (indices indicates \(1,\ldots,p\) populations interest). x vector containing estimates \(\hat{\theta}_1,\ldots,\hat{\theta}_p\) Sigma estimate covariance matrix x. method assumes estimates asymptotically normal sample sizes datasets large enough \(\hat{\theta}-\theta\) approximately distributed \(N(0,\Sigma)\). argument Sigma contain estimate covariance matrix \(\Sigma\). instance, population \(j\) $$\sqrt{n_j} (\hat{\theta}_j-\theta_j) \to_d N(0, \sigma_j^2)$$ datasets population drawn independently , Sigma diagonal matrix $$diag(\hat{\sigma}_1^2/n_1,\ldots,\hat{\sigma}_p^2/n_p)$$ containing estimates asymptotic variances divided sample size. generally, estimates x may dependent, Sigma must estimate covariance matrix including -diagonal terms. Marginal confidence sets (simul=FALSE) confidence set population \(j\) contains true rank population \(j\) probability approximately equal nominal coverage level. Simultaneous confidence sets (simul=TRUE) hand confidence sets populations indicated indices cover true ranks populations simultaneously probability approximately equal nominal coverage level. instance, PISA example , marginal confidence set country \(j\) covers true rank country \(j\) probability approximately equal 0.95. simultaneous confidence set countries covers true ranks countries simultaneously probability approximately equal 0.95. function implements procedures developed described detail Mogstad, Romano, Shaikh, Wilhelm (2023). procedure based testing large family hypotheses pairwise comparisons. Stepwise methods can used improve power procedure , potentially, rejecting hypotheses without violating desired coverage property resulting confidence set. employed stepdown=TRUE. practical point view, stepdown=TRUE computationally demanding, often results tighter confidence sets. procedure uses parametric bootstrap procedure based approximate multivariate normal distribution.

code: x <- seq(1, 3, length = 10) V <- diag(rep(0.04, 10)) CS <- csranks(x, V) grid::current.viewport() #> viewport[ROOT]  plot(CS)  # Equivalent: plotranking(CS$rank, CS$L, CS$U)   # plotranking returns a ggplot object. It can be customized further: library(ggplot2) pl <- plot(CS) pl + xlab("position in ranking") + ylab("population label") + theme_gray()   # horizontal = FALSE uses ggplot2::coord_flip underneath. The x and y axes swap places. pl <- plot(CS, horizontal = FALSE) pl + xlab("position in ranking") + # Note, that xlab refers to vertical axis now   ylab("population label") + theme_gray()
